chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad ibn Sahl, from his father, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام about the mutamattiʿ who enters Makkah on the Day of Tarwiyah. He said: For the mutamattiʿ, there is time until sunset.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim عليه السلام, the authority answering the legal question
key_terms.غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِ: sunset, the stated end point of the time period
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the sacred sanctuary entered for the pilgrimage rites
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the eighth day of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, an important day in the hajj rites

ai.seo_question: Until what time can a pilgrim performing tamattuʿ enter Makkah on the Day of Tarwiyah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the time in which a pilgrim performing tamattuʿ may still catch the rite upon entering Makkah on the Day of Tarwiyah. Imam Mūsā عليه السلام states that the relevant time extends until sunset, indicating the validity of the act within that limit.
